application.name: Sample Storefront
application.scope: This representative contract covers an observed single-page storefront, its API and message-driven order backend, the current telemetry footprint, and the implementation and verification work needed for trustworthy journey observability.
changes: Initial evidence from production behavior, source, architecture diagrams, read-only telemetry queries, and authorized security checks was reconciled into one canonical contract.
The first version defines bounded transactions, exhaustive observed workflows, cross-account propagation, operational detectors, objectives, and an executable work-order queue.
nextSteps: Review architecture and current telemetry before evaluating the recommendations.
Review findings, use cases, workflows, business transactions, and their linked work orders.
Confirm unresolved evidence questions or supply additional source and tenant exports.
Accept this immutable version only after all linked detail and QA evidence is satisfactory.

summaries.architecture: The observed React storefront performs client-side routing from one host bootstrap, calls a Node API in the web account, and publishes accepted requests across a managed event bus to a worker in an integration account before fulfillment.
summaries.technology: Source and response evidence identify React, a client router, Node services, managed cloud messaging, an OpenTelemetry Collector, and a hosted payment dependency, with each technology mapped to its instrumentation consequence.
summaries.currentTelemetry: Browser and service telemetry are present but only partially trusted: automatic spans arrive without stable workflow identity, route values are unbounded, message context breaks at the queue, and logs do not consistently carry trace identifiers.
summaries.findings: The priority finding is a correctness and privacy defect in which raw route and cookie fields reach telemetry before bounded classification and redaction, creating misleading dimensions and avoidable sensitive-data retention.
summaries.strategy: Establish signal trust first, then ship one initialization owner, bounded route and business-transaction classifiers, write-once baggage propagation, explicit message carriers, ordered Collector controls, and operational metrics.
summaries.implementationPath: The dependency path begins with deterministic schema and privacy guardrails, adds browser and backend propagation, instruments the observed order workflows, then creates dashboards, detectors, objectives, release overlays, and portfolio verification.
summaries.workOrders: Three bounded work orders separate the shared contract, end-to-end workflow instrumentation, and operational activation so each repository leg has explicit paths, tests, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and verification.
summaries.useCases: The primary use case follows order submission from the checkout interaction through the API, message producer, cross-account consumer, and fulfillment acknowledgement, exposing errors, p90 latency, silence, and trace-log joins.
summaries.workflows: Two evidence-derived workflows cover payment authorization and order submission rather than generic clicks; each defines its span tree, events, bounded meters, join types, dashboard, detectors, objective, and verification.
summaries.businessTransactions: The checkout business transaction is a bounded global grouping set by the host route classifier and propagated in baggage; its catalogue includes every observed payment and submission intent from source and analytics evidence.
summaries.contracts: Shared contracts specify exactly one provider initialization, host-owned SPA route spans, allowlisted baggage stamping, identity propagation, first-touch attribution, honest join types, Collector ordering, redaction, and cardinality arithmetic.
summaries.operations: The operating model combines a workflow dashboard with p90 latency and release overlays, thresholded error and silent-outage detectors, a rolling success objective with an explicit error budget, Synthetics, path tests, and verification.
summaries.reference: The reference register preserves measured, stated, public, and derived evidence without customer identifiers, records the prior diagram and guide roles, and names unresolved queue-volume and payment-path placement questions.

architecture.narrative: A React single-page storefront owns the only browser provider initialization and classifies client routes before starting navigation spans. The browser calls an order API in the web account; accepted requests publish through a managed event bus and queue to a worker in an integration account, which invokes fulfillment and records an acknowledgement or DLQ failure.

backends.name: Order API
backends.role: Validates order requests, authorizes payment, and publishes accepted orders.
failurePoints: Payment authorization can time out before the order is published.
A successful response can be returned while message publication later fails.

backends.name: Order Worker
backends.role: Consumes accepted orders, invokes fulfillment, records acknowledgement, and routes terminal failures.
failurePoints: Missing message context creates a disconnected trace at the account boundary.
Repeated fulfillment failure sends the message to a dead-letter queue.

accounts.boundary: Hosts the storefront edge and synchronous order API with public ingress.
Hosts message consumers and controlled egress to fulfillment systems.

buses.contextCarrier: Message attributes carry traceparent, tracestate, and the bounded baggage allowlist.
failurePoints: Publish acknowledgement can be absent after the API commits the request.
Consumer retries can exhaust and move the message to the dead-letter queue.

downstreams.role: Reserves inventory and creates the fulfillment request.
downstreams.consequence: Latency or rejection prevents accepted storefront orders from reaching physical fulfillment.

thirdParties.name: Hosted payment gateway
thirdParties.consequence: Its synchronous authorization sits on the submission path and must be separated from internal API latency and failures.
controls: Record only the bounded processor result and never payment credentials.
Use Synthetics for application behavior and path testing for off-box network isolation.

failurePoints.surface: Order API to hosted payment gateway
failurePoints.effect: The shopper cannot submit the order and may retry an operation whose final state is uncertain.
failurePoints.detection: Payment authorization error ratio and p90 duration are grouped by bounded result and deployment environment.

failurePoints.effect: One business journey appears as two healthy traces and Related Content cannot traverse the boundary.
failurePoints.detection: A controlled message verifies a shared trace id and stamped business context on the consumer span.

technology.name: React
technology.versionEvidence: package lock and production chunk signatures
technology.observabilityConsequence: Client transitions need a host-owned listener because document-load spans cover only the initial route.

technology.name: Node.js
technology.observabilityConsequence: The shared SDK bootstrap must install trace context plus baggage before application modules load.

technology.name: Managed messaging
technology.observabilityConsequence: Producers inject and consumers extract message attributes; DLQ redrive links back rather than claiming one parent.

technology.name: OpenTelemetry Collector
technology.versionEvidence: collector deployment values and active pipeline export
technology.observabilityConsequence: Derivation and redaction must precede spanmetrics, while batch remains the final processor before export.

currentTelemetry.observed: Initial document data arrives, but client-route identity is not refreshed and raw route values enter telemetry.
gaps: No bounded page classifier runs on every client transition.
The current route attribute is unsuitable for a long-term metric dimension.

currentTelemetry.observed: Automatic HTTP spans identify services but sampled traces lack stable transaction and workflow attributes.
gaps: No evidence-derived workflow registry is stamped on root and child spans.
The queue consumer begins a disconnected trace after the account crossing.

currentTelemetry.component: Splunk platform logs and Log Observer Connect
currentTelemetry.observed: Application logs are retained in approved indexes, while trace and span identifiers are inconsistent.
gaps: Error rows cannot reliably deep-link into the corresponding APM trace.
Cookie headers require deletion before any log or trace export.

currentTelemetry.observed: No independent checkout canary or public-path test was present in the supplied telemetry inventory.
gaps: A silent route failure has no independent transaction probe.
Payment-provider path failure cannot be separated from application execution.

findings.title: Unbounded route and cookie fields reach telemetry
findings.observed: Authorized payload inspection showed a raw client route used as an attribute and a cookie header present before the current Collector export. The route creates unbounded metric identity, while the cookie field can retain session material that has no observability purpose.
surfaces: Collector trace and log processor configuration
findings.exposure: Telemetry readers and downstream retention systems can receive unnecessary request context from every affected browser session.
findings.risk: Cardinality growth can hide useful workflow series while retained cookie data expands privacy exposure and incident scope.
remediation: Stop exporting the cookie header and remove existing raw-route promotion before adding any new metric dimensions.
Classify routes into the bounded page.type and sample.bt enums in the host listener.
Enforce the deny list and processor ordering in deterministic CI validation.
findings.verification: A controlled route suite must emit only registered page and transaction values, and a search over exported trace and log attributes must return zero cookie headers.

strategy.title: Restore signal trust
strategy.question: Can route, privacy, and service identity be trusted before journey detectors are armed?
strategy.recommendation: Remove forbidden fields, classify every client transition, stabilize service and deployment resources, and validate the exported attribute set before treating error rates or route dimensions as operational truth.

strategy.title: Emit journey identity in code
strategy.question: Which shopper intent and business transaction produced each browser and backend span?
strategy.recommendation: Use a bounded global transaction tag and evidence-derived workflow names, then stamp them from W3C Baggage onto every span so Business Transactions, Tag Spotlight, dashboards, and detectors share one identity.

strategy.title: Continue causal message traces
strategy.question: Did an accepted order cross the account boundary and reach fulfillment without retry or DLQ failure?
strategy.retentionClass: trace context plus bounded custom metrics
strategy.recommendation: Inject traceparent, tracestate, and the baggage allowlist into message attributes, extract before consumer spans, use links for DLQ redrive, and record bounded publish, consume, acknowledgement, and failure meters.

strategy.title: Join traces, logs, releases, and path evidence
strategy.question: Can an engineer distinguish application, deployment, log, and off-box path causes from one workflow view?
strategy.productSurface: Log Observer Connect, Events API, Synthetics, and ThousandEyes
strategy.retentionClass: long-retention logs, release events, and probe results
strategy.recommendation: Write trace and span identifiers into approved logs, overlay deployments, add a checkout transaction canary, and place path tests across the public payment dependency without duplicating application workflow spans.

implementationPhases.title: Trust and deterministic contracts
implementationPhases.outcome: Telemetry is privacy-safe, route and transaction values are bounded, and CI rejects schema drift before journey code ships.
exitCriteria: No exported trace or log contains a cookie header.
Every tested client transition emits a registered page and transaction value.

implementationPhases.title: End-to-end order instrumentation
implementationPhases.outcome: Browser, API, producer, consumer, and fulfillment spans form an honest trace with workflow events and bounded meters.
exitCriteria: A controlled order trace crosses the account boundary with stamped baggage.
Payment and submission metrics expose bounded dimensions and no identity ids.

implementationPhases.title: Operational activation and proof
implementationPhases.outcome: Dashboards, detectors, objectives, releases, logs, Synthetics, and path evidence answer the use-case question.
exitCriteria: Threshold and zero-activity detector inputs are queryable under controlled tests.
Trace-to-log, release overlay, transaction canary, and path isolation checks pass.

workOrders.title: Install deterministic signal contracts
workOrders.outcome: The shared library, route registry, baggage allowlist, redaction order, deny list, and CI gates establish one privacy-safe contract.

changes: Own one provider initialization and install bounded route plus baggage contracts.
tests: Run route classifier, one-init, baggage allowlist, and deny-list tests.

changes: Order derivation and redaction before spanmetrics and batch export.
tests: Validate Collector configuration and assert forbidden attributes are absent.

acceptanceCriteria: Only the host bootstrap initializes the browser provider.
Every schema key has cardinality and propagation metadata.
Raw route and cookie fields fail deterministic validation.
verification: Exercise each registered route and inspect bounded page and transaction tags.
Query exported spans and logs for the deny list and require zero matches.

workOrders.title: Instrument the order journey
workOrders.outcome: The API, message producer, consumer, and fulfillment call emit the registered workflows, events, metrics, and honest joins.

changes: Add workflow helpers, payment events, message inject and extract, DLQ links, and bounded meters.
tests: Run HTTP propagation, message continuation, DLQ link, event, and metric dimension tests.

acceptanceCriteria: The controlled order has one trace through the normal message path.
DLQ redrive creates a new trace linked to the original rather than changing its parent.
verification: Inspect the trace tree, event attributes, and baggage stamp on the consumer.
Query all proposed metric dimensions and verify bounded values.

workOrders.title: Activate operational views and proof
workOrders.outcome: The workflow dashboard, detectors, objective, release events, logs, transaction canary, and public-path test are reviewable.

changes: Create reviewable configuration and read-only verification for every operational object.
tests: Validate configuration, run fixture queries, and execute controlled detector input tests.

acceptanceCriteria: Every dashboard panel and detector uses an eligible metric dimension.
The objective calculates its target and explicit rolling error budget.
Release, log, Synthetics, and path evidence link from the workflow view.
verification: Run each verification criterion and preserve query provenance.
Keep all tenant mutations subject to independent human review and apply.

useCases.title: Order submission
useCases.narrative: A shopper authorizes payment and submits an order from the checkout route. The API publishes the accepted request across an account boundary, the worker invokes fulfillment, and operations must distinguish payment, publish, consume, fulfillment, and silent-market failures.
useCases.question: Did the shopper's accepted order reach fulfillment within the objective, and where did a failure or latency regression occur?

joins.reason: The synchronous request is one causal operation and must remain in the same trace tree.
One accepted order message causes one consumer operation on the normal processing path.
Redrive starts later in a new execution, so claiming the old consumer as its parent would be false.
The order identifier is a high-cardinality troubleshooting key and never a metric dimension.

verification: Submit a controlled order and confirm the browser, API, producer, consumer, and fulfillment spans are queryable together.
Force payment rejection, publish failure, and a held message to prove the error and silent-outage signals.

workflows.name: checkout.payment.authorize
workflows.narrative: The shopper submits payment details to the hosted payment flow, and the Order API records only the bounded authorization outcome and duration.

events.name: checkout.payment.completed
events.when: When the bounded authorization result is known

metrics.name: sample.checkout.payment
metrics.purpose: Count payment attempts and bounded outcomes.

metrics.name: sample.checkout.payment.duration
metrics.purpose: Measure authorization latency independently from order processing.

joins.reason: The browser request and authorization are one synchronous causal request.

verification: A controlled authorization exposes started and completed events with no payment credential fields.
The p90 duration query groups only by the approved environment, market, and provider dimensions.

workflows.name: checkout.order.submit
workflows.narrative: The accepted browser request publishes one order message, continues through the worker, invokes fulfillment, and records acknowledgement or a linked DLQ redrive.

events.name: checkout.order.accepted
events.when: After validation and before message publication

events.name: checkout.order.fulfilled
events.when: After the downstream acknowledges the fulfillment request

metrics.name: sample.order.submission
metrics.purpose: Count accepted, failed, and fulfilled orders without identity dimensions.

metrics.name: sample.order.end-to-end.duration
metrics.purpose: Measure accepted-to-fulfillment duration across the message boundary.

joins.reason: One message causes one consumer operation and the extracted parent is truthful.
The delayed redrive is a new execution that points backward without changing parentage.

verification: A controlled message keeps one trace id from producer through fulfillment and carries the allowlisted baggage keys.
A DLQ redrive starts a new trace with a link to the original and increments only bounded failure dimensions.

businessTransactions.name: Checkout
businessTransactions.summary: The checkout surface owns payment authorization and order submission intents discovered in route components, analytics events, API clients, and the order sequence diagram.
businessTransactions.whereSet: The host route classifier sets sample.bt when navigation enters any registered checkout route.
businessTransactions.propagation: The value becomes a global browser attribute and bounded baggage entry stamped onto backend and consumer spans.
businessTransactions.tenantRule: APM groups traces using the bounded global tag sample.bt after its approved MetricSet indexing check.
businessTransactions.verification: Navigate every checkout route and query Tag Spotlight for only the registered checkout value on browser and backend spans.

contracts.singleInit: The host bootstrap is the only artifact that initializes browser telemetry, installs the allowlisted stamp processor, captures attribution, and subscribes to route changes. Route modules consume the shared API and never initialize another provider or application name.

spaRoutes.classifier: The pure classifier maps known route families to catalog, checkout, confirmation, or unknown-safe enums; raw paths remain trace-only and never become dimensions.

attributes.name: sample.bt
attributes.setAt: initial route and every client navigation

attribution.trigger: The host captures attribution exactly once per browser session after consent and before the first workflow request.
attribution.firstTouch: Persist the first bounded source and medium in local storage for cross-session comparison.
attribution.lastTouch: Persist the current bounded source and medium in session storage for the active order journey.

joins.reason: The browser request and server handler are the same causal operation.
The normal consumer work is caused by exactly one accepted order message.
The delayed retry begins a new execution and must not claim the original parent.
The identity key supports troubleshooting but is too high-cardinality for a metric dimension.

collector.placement: A gateway Collector receives browser and service OTLP before the Observability Cloud and approved log exporters.
collector.ottl:
processors:
  transform/derive:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
      - context: span
        statements:
          - set(attributes["sample.market"], "DEFAULT") where attributes["sample.market"] == nil
          - set(attributes["page.type"], "other") where attributes["page.type"] == nil
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [memory_limiter, transform/derive, attributes/redact, spanmetrics, batch]

redactions.reason: Cookie material has no approved observability purpose.
Troubleshooting requires stable comparison without retaining raw email.
Network grouping needs only the approved coarse prefix.

dashboards.title: Order submission
panels: Submission rate, error percentage, and explicit p90 end-to-end duration.
Payment authorization result and p90 duration by bounded provider.
Producer, consumer, fulfillment, retry, and dead-letter counts.
Trace deep link, Log Observer Connect results, and release-event overlay.
dashboards.signalFlow:
total = data('sample.order.submission', filter=filter('deployment.environment', 'prod')).sum(by=['sample.market'])
failed = data('sample.order.submission', filter=filter('deployment.environment', 'prod') and filter('status', 'failed')).sum(by=['sample.market'])
(failed / total * 100).publish(label='order error percent by market')

detectors.name: Order error rate
detectors.threshold: failed divided by total greater than 2 percent
detectors.runbook: Compare payment, publish, consume, and fulfillment panels before selecting the owning response path.
detectors.verification: Inject one bounded failure outcome in a controlled environment and verify the detector input crosses its threshold.

detectors.name: Order silent outage
detectors.threshold: zero accepted orders after a nonzero historical baseline
detectors.runbook: Check the transaction canary, RUM route traffic, public path, and API health before treating silence as demand.
detectors.verification: Hold controlled messages for one market fixture and verify zero activity triggers without grouping by an identity key.

objectives.name: Successful order fulfillment
objectives.sli: Fulfilled orders divided by accepted order submissions with controlled retries counted once.
objectives.errorBudget: 0.5 percent, equal to 216 minutes of equivalent unavailability in 30 days
objectives.verification: Recompute numerator and denominator from the same bounded metric and compare a controlled success and failure fixture.

operations.releaseCorrelation: The deployment job posts one event after a healthy release with service.name, service.version, and deployment.environment; every RED panel overlays matching events.

synthetics.evidence: The public checkout route and order API create an application-level canary question independent of real-user traffic.
synthetics.design: Run a non-destructive checkout transaction using fixture inventory and stop before any irreversible fulfillment side effect.

thousandEyes.evidence: The shopper, CDN, public origin, and hosted payment gateway create off-box DNS, ISP, CDN, and SaaS path questions.
thousandEyes.design: Use HTTP and transaction path tests from representative cloud regions to distinguish path degradation from application execution.

operations.logCorrelation: Approved application logs carry trace_id, span_id, service.name, service.version, deployment.environment, workflow.name, and sample.market after redaction, enabling Log Observer Connect in both directions.

verificationCriteria.criterion: Every client transition has bounded page and transaction identity.
verificationCriteria.method: Exercise the registered route fixture and query RUM spans by page.type and sample.bt.
verificationCriteria.expected: Only catalog, checkout, confirmation, and other values appear; no raw route is a dimension.

verificationCriteria.criterion: The normal order message continues one trace across accounts.
verificationCriteria.method: Submit a controlled order and inspect producer and consumer parentage plus stamped baggage.
verificationCriteria.expected: Producer and consumer share one trace id and the consumer contains the allowlisted context.

verificationCriteria.criterion: Trace and log records join without retaining forbidden fields.
verificationCriteria.method: Open an error trace, follow Related Content to logs, and search both products for the deny list.
verificationCriteria.expected: The log opens by trace id and cookie-header searches return zero results.

verificationCriteria.criterion: Operational signals detect errors, silence, releases, and public-path failures.
verificationCriteria.method: Run controlled error and hold tests, publish a release event, and execute the canary plus path probe.
verificationCriteria.expected: Each signal appears in its intended product and links back to the workflow dashboard.

sources: Authorized production response and route behavior capture.
Application source, dependency lock, configuration, analytics events, and tests.

priorArtifacts: The prior architecture diagram supplied account, bus, downstream, and failure-boundary evidence.
